parathyroid hormone produces a significant phosphaturic action and a marked increase of urinary calcium excretion in vitamin D-priming rats.
parathyroid hormone is ineffective in producing a phosphaturic response in vitamin D-deficiency and that vitamin D potentiates the phosphaturic effect of parathyroid in the rat.

parathyroid hormone has no effect on serum calcium concentration in vitamin D-depleted rats, but does so in vitamin D-priming rats, that parathyroid-hormone induced phosphaturia is dependent on the presence of vitamin D, and that serum magnesium concentrations are inversely related to serum phosphate concentrations in rats.

the interrelation of vitamin D and parathyroid hormone in their effects on calcium phosphorus and magnesium homeostasis in the rat.
the interaction of the hormones, vitamin D and parathyroid hormone, and their effects upon calcium, phosphate and magnesium homeostasis.
the interaction of vitamin D and parathyroid hormone on calcium phosphorus and magnesium metabolism in the vitamin D-deficient, vitamin D-priming, and vitamin D-pretreated animals.

vitamin D is essential for the full expression of parathyroid function in the rat.

parathyroid hormone is not a primary factor in calcium mobilization in the absence of an adequate vitamin D level.

vitamin D and parathyroid hormone interact at the cellular level to regulate the concentration of calcium in the serum.
